title: Throughput harness protocol — alpha notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures an alpha-level, reproducible protocol for throughput benchmarking of the serving runtime. Goal: get stable, comparable per-model throughput numbers that reflect realistic request shapes while minimizing noise from cold-starts, host-level jitter, and transient autoscaling.

Scope and non-goals:
- Focus: steady-state throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) for GPU-backed model endpoints.
- Non-goal: micro-optimizing kernel-level flops — that's a different harness.
- We intentionally include batching and KV-cache effects (it's production-relevant).

Hardware/software baseline (record every run):
- Instance type(s): e.g., g4dn.12xlarge (8xA100) or private cluster nodetype (nvidia-a100-40gb).
- Driver + CUDA: record exact versions.
- Runtime build: git sha + build flags (e.g., -O3, cuda compute capability target).
- Model artifact: name, tokenizer version, quantization profile.

Key principles:
1) Keep test surface small: pin model version, config, and data split.
2) Warmup until both latency and GPU utilization stabilize (quantified below).
3) Use long steady-state windows (>= 5 minutes) to smooth noise.
4) Report percentiles and variability across repeated runs.
5) Automate telemetry collection (nvml, dmesg, perf, pprof traces).

Load generator configuration (recommended fields):
- request_shape: {"prompt_length": int, "max_new_tokens": int, "temperature": float}  -- our files will include a small set of canonical shapes (short-chat, mid-doc, long-context).
- arrival_process: poisson | fixed | closed-loop (closed-loop = concurrency-driven).
- concurrency: integer (number of simultaneous outstanding requests).
- qps_target: float (used with poisson arrival).
- batching_hint: optional (max_batch_size).
- kv_cache_mode: cold | warm | partial (see warmup).

Canonical request shapes (examples):
- short-chat: prompt 32 tokens, max_new_tokens 64, typical response length ~40 tokens
- mid-doc: prompt 256 tokens, max_new_tokens 512
- long-context: prompt 2048 tokens, max_new_tokens 512

Warmup strategy (explicit):
- Phase 0 (startup): deploy and wait for node agent ready.
- Phase 1 (priming): run 5–10 minutes of low-rate requests (short-chat) to populate caches, JIT kernels, and to get initial GPU memory warmed.
- Phase 2 (ramp): linearly ramp QPS from 10% to target over 2–5 minutes.
- Phase 3 (hold-in): hold at target for N minutes until metrics converge (see convergence tests).
- Phase 4 (measurement): run measurement window of at least 5 minutes (prefer 10) and collect metrics.

Convergence tests (automated):
- GPU utilization: rolling 30s mean change < 2 percentage points for 3 consecutive windows.
- p50 latency drift: < 3% over 2 consecutive 60s windows.
- Batch size distribution stable: < 5% change in batch counts per bucket.
If not converged after 15 minutes total, abort and mark run failed.

Repeatability and statistics:
- Each configuration = 3 independent runs (fresh restart between runs to capture deployment variabilities).
- For each run report: mean tokens/sec, median requests/sec, p50/p90/p99 latencies (generation-only and end-to-end), GPU util mean/std, avg batch size, error rate.
- Aggregate across runs: report median of means and coefficient of variation (CoV). If CoV > 7% for primary metric, extend runs to 5.
- Use bootstrap to compute 95% CI for tokens/sec.

Telemetry & artifacts to capture (minimum):
- Server logs (structured), including per-request metadata (model_version, batch_id, seq_lengths).
- GPU metrics: NVML sampling (1s), per-GPU memory, sm_util, power.
- OS metrics: iostat, vmstat, dstat (1s sampling for measurement window).
- Runtime traces: pprof/trace for CPU hot paths, kernel traces for attention kernels when practical.
- Loadgen traces: client timestamps, client->server RTT, request IDs.
- System-level network counters if cross-node (tc, ethtool stats).

Load patterns to run (minimal suite):
- Poisson arrival at target QPS (to model open loop traffic).
- Closed-loop concurrency: set concurrency equal to production target and observe achieved QPS.
- Batch-saturation test: artificially set qps high to force max batching and measure degradation.
- Cold-cache run: full cold caches + single short run to quantify cold-start penalty.

Example run checklist (pre-flight):
- [ ] Pin model artifact and build sha in run metadata.
- [ ] Ensure cluster is otherwise idle (no other tenants).
- [ ] Clear caches if doing cold-cache test (restart serving processes).
- [ ] Sync clocks across hosts (chrony/ntp).
- [ ] Reserve monitoring stack and logging sinks.

Example loadgen command (pseudo):
- loadgen --model-url https://... --arrival poisson --qps 420 --shape short-chat --concurrency 64 --duration 15m --trace-out run1234.tar
- For closed-loop: loadgen --mode closed-loop --concurrency 128 --duration 10m --shape mid-doc

Interpretation notes and pitfalls:
- Don’t trust single-run peak QPS. Short spikes happen due to background consolidation. Use steady-state windows.
- KV-cache warmup vs model warmup confounds: long-context models with large KV caches will show high initial mem and lower throughput until cache warmed; document what warmup used.
- Batching artifacts: if a policy uses adaptive batching, you must record batch size histograms. Two runs with same config but slightly different token distribution can produce different batching behaviour; keep token-distribution fixed.
- GPU-runaway: long synthetic runs have produced kernel OOM due to left-over KV fragments — include pre-run mem-check.

Troubleshooting quick wins:
- High p99 but good p50: look for straggler batches (rare large batch causing head-of-line blocking).
- Low GPU util but low throughput: check data loader bottleneck, tokenizer CPU cost, and RPC thread starvation.
- Large variance across runs: confirm no autoscaler events, no node churn, and consistent driver/firmware.

Post-run report minimal fields (JSON-friendly):
- run_id, config_ref, model_sha, qps_target, tokens_per_sec_mean, tokens_per_sec_ci, p50_latency_ms, p90_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, gpu_util_mean, avg_batch_size, error_rate_percent, artifacts_link

Open questions / next steps (alpha):
- Define canonical synthetic prompt set for cross-team comparability.
- Add automated diff script that compares two runs and highlights perf regressions beyond configurable thresholds.
- Integrate with console dashboards so results can be published as per-route perf profiles.

Notes to self (TODO):
- Try an A/B run where batcher policy is toggled (aggressive vs conservative) and measure tail-latency trade-offs.
- Validate that batching histograms are reproducible with same RNG seeds in loadgen.

End of doc.
